title: Schedule of Benefits — RideLink Levels of Service, Vehicles and Assessment Terms
content:
Non-Emergency Medical Transportation is held at one of six RideLink levels of service. This schedule states, for every level, whom the level serves, the vehicle or mode used, the assistance the driver gives, and the assessment and certification terms that attach to the level.

## Who each level serves

| Level | Mobility level served | Further entry condition |
|---|---|---|
| RideLink Transit Pass | Independent | Fixed-route transit within walking distance |
| RideLink Mileage Reimbursement | Independent or assisted | A household vehicle and driver are available |
| RideLink Ambulatory Sedan | Ambulatory | Cannot use fixed-route transit |
| RideLink Door-to-Door Assist | Ambulatory with hands-on assistance | — |
| RideLink Wheelchair Van | Wheelchair user | Wheelchair use documented |
| RideLink Stretcher Van | Must travel lying flat | Physician certification |

## Vehicle, assistance and assessment terms

| Level | Vehicle or mode | Driver assistance | Reassessed within (months after the mobility assessment date) | Physician certification of medical need required | Certification stays valid (calendar days) | Mobility assessment completed within (business days after the request) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RideLink Transit Pass | Fixed-route transit | None | 12 | No | 0 | 5 |
| RideLink Mileage Reimbursement | Member's household vehicle | None | 12 | No | 0 | 5 |
| RideLink Ambulatory Sedan | Sedan | Curb to curb | 12 | No | 0 | 5 |
| RideLink Door-to-Door Assist | Sedan or minivan | Door to door | 12 | No | 0 | 5 |
| RideLink Wheelchair Van | Wheelchair-accessible van | Door to door | 12 | No | 0 | 3 |
| RideLink Stretcher Van | Stretcher van | Door through door | 6 | Yes | 180 | 3 |

A certification validity of 0 days appears on the levels that require no physician certification.

## Reading the schedule

- **Which levels give hands-on driver help?** RideLink Door-to-Door Assist and RideLink Wheelchair Van give door-to-door assistance; RideLink Stretcher Van gives door-through-door assistance; RideLink Ambulatory Sedan is curb to curb; the transit and mileage levels involve no driver assistance.
- **Which level has the shortest reassessment cycle?** RideLink Stretcher Van, reassessed within 6 months of the mobility assessment date; every other level is reassessed within 12 months.
- **Which levels complete a mobility assessment fastest?** RideLink Wheelchair Van and RideLink Stretcher Van, within 3 business days of the request; the other four levels within 5 business days.

*Hypothetical illustration:* a benefit on RideLink Stretcher Van whose mobility assessment date is 10 March is due for reassessment within 6 months of that date, and its trips rely on a physician certification that stays valid for 180 calendar days.
